descriptionWindows: Strip down Windows — remove telemetry, bloatware, and unnecessary services
descriptionOther: Harden your system — manage privacy settings and unnecessary services

privacy.pageDescription: Control telemetry, ads, tracking, and data collection across your system
privacy.emptyStateDescription: Click "Scan" to audit your privacy and security settings and apply recommended hardening.
privacy.adminWarning: Some settings require administrator privileges to modify. Run Clarity as administrator for full protection.
privacy.ipcCallFailed: IPC call failed — try running as administrator
privacy.overviewHint: Protection coverage and overall privacy score
privacy.categoriesHint: Click a category to review and manage individual settings
privacy.recommendationsHint: Top actions to strengthen your privacy
privacy.allProtectedDescription: Your system is fully hardened — no recommended actions.
privacy.activityEmpty: No privacy scans yet — run one to see activity here.
privacy.actionRestoreDesc: Revert all protections to system defaults
privacy.restoreConfirmDescription: This will revert all reversible privacy protections back to their Windows defaults. Non-reversible settings will be skipped.
privacy.restoreFailedToast: Some settings failed to restore — administrator privileges may be required
privacy.restoreNoneToast: Nothing to restore — all settings are already at defaults

privacyCategories.telemetryDescription: Control diagnostic and usage data collection
privacyCategories.adsDescription: Block promoted apps, ad suggestions, and lock screen spotlight
privacyCategories.searchDescription: Keep searches local and disable web-based search features
privacyCategories.syncDescription: Control clipboard syncing, settings sync, and device tracking
privacyCategories.servicesDescription: Disable background services that collect and upload telemetry
privacyCategories.tasksDescription: Disable telemetry scheduled tasks running in the background
privacyCategories.kernelDescription: Kernel security parameters and memory protection via sysctl
privacyCategories.networkDescription: Network stack hardening and traffic filtering via sysctl
privacyCategories.accessDescription: Access control policies, SSH hardening, and system restrictions
privacyCategories.aiDescription: Disable Copilot, Recall, and other AI features that analyze your data
privacyCategories.browserDescription: Stop browsers from reporting usage data to Microsoft, Google, and Mozilla

debloater.pageDescription: Remove pre-installed Windows apps and OEM bloatware
debloater.irreversibleWarning: Irreversible — Removed apps can only be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store. Review selections carefully.
debloater.emptyStateDescription: Click "Scan" to find pre-installed apps and OEM bloatware.
debloater.confirmDescription: This will permanently remove {{count}} app(s). They can be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store if needed.
debloater.scanFailedError: Failed to scan for bloatware. Make sure PowerShell is available.
debloater.removeFailedError: Failed to remove some apps. Administrator privileges may be required.

serviceManager.pageDescription: View, manage, and disable unnecessary Windows services — or turn a disabled one back on
serviceManager.infoBannerUseRecommended: Use "Apply Recommended" for a safe one-click preset.
serviceManager.infoBannerReEnable: Select a disabled service to turn it back on.
serviceManager.emptyStateDescription: Enumerate all services and identify which ones can be safely disabled to improve performance.
serviceManager.overviewHint: Overall posture of your running services and what can be safely turned off
serviceManager.listHint: Search, filter, and act on services — select a row or use the row action
serviceManager.recHint: High-value hardening actions based on this scan
serviceManager.recUnnecessaryDescription: Safe to disable — running in the background without a clear benefit.
serviceManager.recHighRiskDescription: High-risk services are active. Only disable them if you understand the consequences.
serviceManager.recAllGoodDescription: Your running services are already well trimmed. Nothing to do here.
serviceManager.activityHint: What has been disabled, enabled, and changed over time
serviceManager.activityTrendNoData: No activity yet — run a scan and apply changes to see a trend.
serviceManager.actionScanDesc: Enumerate all services and classify risk
serviceManager.actionRefreshDesc: Re-run the scan for a fresh state
serviceManager.confirmDescription: This will disable {{count}} service(s) and stop any that are currently running. This requires administrator privileges.
serviceManager.confirmEnableDescription: This will set {{count}} disabled service(s) back to {{startType}}. Automatic services are started right away. This requires administrator privileges.

firewall.pageDescription: Review inbound firewall rules and flag anything suspicious, exposed, or left over from removed software
firewall.overviewHint: Overall posture of your inbound firewall rules
firewall.profilesHint: Which network profiles inbound rules apply to
firewall.rulesHint: Search, filter, and act on inbound allow rules
firewall.showBuiltinTitle: Microsoft / system / packaged-app rules hidden by default — these ship with Windows and shouldn't be removed.
firewall.noRulesMatchDesc: Try adjusting your filters or search query.
firewall.truncatedNotice: This scan finished early, so the list below is incomplete. Rescan to audit every rule.
firewall.findingsHint: High-value hardening actions from this audit
firewall.recFirewallInactiveDescription: No front-end firewall is running and no filter chain is blocking inbound traffic. Incoming connections are accepted on all ports.
firewall.recStaleTitle: {{count}} rule{{plural}} point at a missing program
firewall.recStaleDescription: Leftover rules from uninstalled or moved software. Safe to remove.
firewall.recUnsignedDescription: Inbound rules backed by unsigned executables are easy to spoof.
firewall.recBroadScopeDescription: Any remote address, any port, on public profiles — a wide exposure.
firewall.recAllGoodDescription: Nothing needs attention in this audit.
firewall.recDefaultDenyDescription: No inbound allow rules were reported — the cleanest possible posture.
firewall.activityHint: Latest audit summary and where the findings are
firewall.activityTrendNoData: Run an audit to populate findings.
firewall.actionAuditDesc: Enumerate inbound rules and classify risk
firewall.actionRefreshDesc: Re-run the audit for a fresh state
firewall.confirmDisableDescription: Disable {{count}} rule{{plural}}. You can re-enable them later from your firewall settings.
firewall.confirmDeleteDescription: Permanently delete {{count}} rule{{plural}}. This cannot be undone.
firewall.noScanDescription: Scan to review inbound firewall rules and flag anything suspicious.
